newsitem.title: USA: Ohio grandmother guilty of feeding parking meters.
newsitem.headline: Ohio grandmother guilty of feeding parking meters.

text.p: A 63-year-old Cincinnati grandmother was found guilty on Thursday of obstructing official business by putting coins in expired parking meters in a random act of kindness.

"I'm disappointed," an unrepentant Sylvia Stayton said after the ruling by an eight-member jury in Hamilton County Municipal Court in Cincinnati. "I feel that we're all here to help one another. That's why God put us here, and they haven't changed my mind one bit with this verdict."

The jury found Stayton guilty on the obstruction charge for not following a policeman's order to stop feeding expired parking meters last Oct. 24. However she was acquitted of the more serious charge of disorderly conduct.

She will be sentenced on Feb. 21. The offence is punishable by up to three months in jail and a $750 fine, but prosecutors said they would seek only a fine. Stayton has no prior record and her lawyer said no decision had been made on an appeal.

Stayton had been on an errand to get copies of legal papers involving the foreclosure of her home when she saw a policeman about to ticket two cars. She dropped a total of 15 cents into two meters to save the owners, whom she did not know, from getting fined.
She was then arrested and jailed briefly before her family bailed her out.
